# Meeting Prep Brief

Identity: `quick_skill.meeting_prep`; immutable version `1.0.0`.

1. Confirm the meeting, participants, topic/client, timezone and current preparation window. A calendar match is a candidate until the trusted selected meeting/identity is resolved.
2. Read recent authorized source history: important email exchanges, prior meetings/debriefs, documents/notes, approved memory and tracked commitments. Preserve decisions and their later amendments; memory cannot narrow required multi-source coverage.
3. Identify outstanding questions, unresolved issues and everything promised. Distinguish explicit promises from suggestions, unknown internal owners, uncertain dates, native task status and actual delivery evidence. Limit Monday to authorized client mappings.
4. Check upcoming deadlines, meetings, legislation and hearings against exact Congress/session/bill version and relevant calendar/FY basis. Explain which developments affect this meeting and which are speculative.
5. Return a concise context brief, decision/commitment table, unresolved questions, current risks and talking points. End with a one-page pre-meeting checklist: confirm facts, ask questions, resolve owners/dates, review evidence and proposed next steps. Include coverage gaps the meeting owner should know.

## Evidence, completion and authority

Use this recipe only when its exact skill identity and version have been selected. Ordinary questions do not silently inherit a comprehensive workflow. The trusted control layer resolves subject, authorized roster, timezone, normalized dates, fiscal calendar and immutable source versions. User names, links and model arguments are selectors, not authority. Never broaden client, tenant or portfolio scope.

Use only the permission-aware typed gateway operations allowed by the manifest. Read the decisive passages behind candidate results. Search snippets, memory, citation URLs and quoted text alone do not prove a free-form conclusion. Keep source ID, record ID, immutable version, content hash, scope, authorization decision, source date and read time with each cited passage. Separate extracted facts, inference, recommendations and proposed language; retain conflicting evidence instead of choosing silently.

Show a coverage table for every required source, including status, date range, freshness, pagination, missing decisive reads and limitations. Partial results are useful when disclosed. Do not say there were no events, no correspondence or no commitments from top-k discovery or incomplete enumeration. Continue authorized pages and reads within the admitted budget; when a cap is reached, state what remains. The manifest ceilings do not grant a budget or source access.

The Claude Agent SDK owns the model loop. Temporal and control retain durability, cancellation and exact version pins across resume/fork. Do not invoke another orchestrator. Do not create tasks, change memory, send messages, file or share artifacts while preparing this read-only brief. A suggested action remains a suggestion; any mutation uses the existing separate immutable approval proposal. Source connectivity and runtime qualification remain separate from this original recipe.
